faq.a: Yes. Every result — coins, dice, random numbers, Yes/No/Maybe and the wheel — uses crypto.getRandomValues, the browser's cryptographically secure generator, with rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias. Unlike Math.random it isn't seedable or predictable. The coin and dice statistics view charts your observed frequencies against the expected fair frequency, so you can watch results converge over many trials.

faq.q: What's in it besides a coin flip?
faq.a: A dice roller (D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20, D100), up to six at once with a modifier and dice-notation input like 3d6+2; a random number generator with min, max, count and an allow-duplicates toggle; a Yes/No/Maybe decider; and a custom spin wheel you fill with one option per line. A statistics chart and a session history tie them together.

faq.q: Can I flip several coins at once and track the totals?
faq.a: Yes — choose 1, 2, 3, 5 or 10 coins and each flip shows how many heads and tails came up. Running totals and percentages accumulate across the session and persist in your browser (coinSession), so you can run hundreds of flips to see the percentages approach 50/50. Reset Stats clears just the coin tally.

faq.q: What does the dice-notation field accept?
faq.a: It parses the standard NdS±M form, for example 3d6+2 meaning three six-sided dice plus two. The number of dice is capped at 1–100 and sides at 2–1000; anything outside that or malformed notation is rejected with a prompt. Each roll is added to the session history, which you can copy or clear, and feeds the distribution chart.
